# requireNonSymbol

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a symbol.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonSymbol() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a symbol. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonSymbol<T>(
  value: T | symbol,
  message: string = "Expected a non-symbol value."
): T;
```

Registered symbols from `Symbol.for` and the well-known symbols both pass; nothing else does.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                 | Type          | Description                                                   |
| :-------------------------------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                   | `T \| symbol` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-symbol value."` | `string`      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with a symbol excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition              |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a symbol. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonSymbol("id"); // => "id"
requireNonSymbol(null); // => null
requireNonSymbol(Symbol("id")); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonSymbol(Symbol.iterator); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
